newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banacci Q1 1997 profit 971 mln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Banacci Q1 1997 profit 971 mln pesos.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival (Banacci) reported on Wednesday a total profit of 971 million pesos in the first quarter, and its bank subsidiary Banamex had a net gain of 389 million pesos.

Banacci said the results for the first time were reported under U.S. GAAP accounting standards, and that comparisons with previous quarters were invalid. However, it did include them: Banacci Q1 1996 net under old accounting rules was 508 million pesos and Banamex's profit was 576 million pesos.

Banamex's capitalization index was about 15 percent at the end of the quarter, compared with 12.6 percent on December 31, the group said. The bank's level of reserves against past-due loans was 59 percent.
Banacci said Banamex's result included a charge of 87 million pesos as a result of its net monetary position.
Accival, its brokerage unit, showed a net profit of 42 million pesos, including a charge of 30 million pesos for its net monetary position.
Its insurance arm, Seguros Banamex-AEGON, had a net gain of 44 million pesos, almost double the 23 million pesos in Q1 1996, it said.
Banamex's index of past-due loans net of reserves was 9.5 percent, while its gross past-due loans were 20.5 percent.

The banking group said it had raised 27 percent of the four billion pesos of capital that it pledged to muster this year in exchange for the sale of Banamex loans to the Bank Insurance Fund (Fobaproa) in December.
The funds came from the sale of Banamex Investment Bank in London, and from dividends from its subsidiaries California Commerce Bank, Accival and Seguros Banamex-AEGON, it said.

It said its estimated 15 percent capitalization ratio did not include capital from Banamex Investment Bank nor the insurance unit. Had it included them, the ratio would have been 15.6 percent on March 31, it said.
